prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset: one 4:3 landscape painting for The Burnt Book Sanskrit learning story. Request 1536 x 1152 native output or the closest supported native 4:3 resolution. Refined Indian watercolor with restrained gouache on warm ivory paper; organic detail, quiet ochre, sage, dusty terracotta, muted indigo. Warm, gentle, evocative storytelling, consistent character design.
Canonical scene brief: Children huddled together in a lamplit school hall while a storm hammers the shutters, a small girl clinging to the old Ācārya who sits among them; at the window a grinning grey-green spirit pressing its face against the shutter slats.
Character appearances:
you: Always seen from behind or at a distance, face never detailed, so every learner can be the hero: a young person in a simple ochre kurta with a cloth shoulder bag.
dadi: A warm, sharp-eyed grandmother in her seventies, silver hair in a low bun, round spectacles, a cream cotton sari with a thin maroon border and a grey shawl; carries a cloth-bound notebook.
shuka: A bright green rose-ringed parrot with a red beak and a faint pink and black neck ring, a little scruffy, very expressive eyes; usually on your shoulder or Dādī's.
acarya: A very old, serene scholar with a white beard and a saffron shawl, a palm-leaf manuscript always under his arm, kind half-closed eyes.
vayuka: A swirling grey-green spirit made of wind and leaves, with a wide windblown smile.
Phone-first composition: clear compact narrative grouping, essential faces, hands and objects comfortably inside all edges. Show the complete scene without border. No collage or multi-panel layout.
MANDATORY TEXT OVERRIDE: this card authorizes NO writing in the painting. Where the scene brief or character description mentions letters, a register, script, writing, numbers, sacred symbols or letter-shaped objects, show the corresponding physical door, pillar, book, leaf, crown or cord WITHOUT any letters or letterlike marks. Use purely floral carvings and completely blank smooth manuscript surfaces. Teaching letters remain separate live app text. No typography, numerals, Om signs, invented script, explanatory marks, sound lines, watermark or labels anywhere.

image.brief: Children huddled together in a lamplit school hall while a storm hammers the shutters, a small girl clinging to the old Ācārya who sits among them; at the window a grinning grey-green spirit pressing its face against the shutter slats.

alt.en: Children huddle in a school hall during a storm with a grinning wind spirit at the window
alt.hi: आँधी में पाठशाला के कक्ष में दुबके बच्चे और खिड़की पर मुस्कुराता पवन-भूत

narration.en: Everyone crowds into the school hall as the storm hammers the shutters. Children huddle. A small girl whispers: “I am afraid of the thunder.” The Ācārya sits down among them. “What you fear, Sanskrit puts in the fifth case, as if you were backing away from it.” Outside, the wind spirit presses a grinning face to the window.
narration.hi: आँधी खिड़कियों के किवाड़ों पर प्रहार करती है और सब पाठशाला के कक्ष में सिमट आते हैं। बच्चे दुबक जाते हैं। एक नन्ही बालिका फुसफुसाती है, “मुझे बादल की गड़गड़ाहट से डर लगता है।” आचार्य उनके बीच बैठ जाते हैं। “जिससे डरो उसे संस्कृत पञ्चमी में रखती है, मानो तुम उससे पीछे हट रहे हो।” बाहर पवन-भूत खिड़की पर मुस्कुराता चेहरा सटा देता है।

body.en: With verbs of fear and protection, the thing feared or guarded against stands in the fifth case: {{व्याघ्रात् बिभेति}} (he fears the tiger), {{बालकं सर्पात् रक्षति}} (he protects the boy from the snake).
body.hi: भय और रक्षा की क्रियाओं के साथ जिससे भय हो या रक्षा की जाए वह पञ्चमी में आता है: {{व्याघ्रात् बिभेति}} (वह बाघ से डरता है), {{बालकं सर्पात् रक्षति}} (वह बालक को साँप से बचाता है)।

meaning.en: He protects the boy from the snake.
meaning.hi: वह बालक को साँप से बचाता है।

body.en: To say “more than”, put the thing compared with in the fifth case and add {{तर}} to the quality: {{रामात् श्यामः दीर्घतरः}}, “Śyāma is taller than Rāma”. The ending {{तर}} means “more”.
body.hi: ‘से अधिक’ कहने के लिए जिससे तुलना हो उसे पञ्चमी में रखिए और गुण में {{तर}} जोड़िए: {{रामात् श्यामः दीर्घतरः}}, ‘श्याम राम से लम्बा है’। प्रत्यय {{तर}} का अर्थ ‘अधिक’ है।

prompt.en: “The boy fears the tiger.” Which word for “tiger”?
prompt.hi: ‘बालक बाघ से डरता है।’ ‘बाघ’ के लिए कौन-सा रूप?

explain.en: What is feared takes the fifth case.
explain.hi: जिससे डर लगे वह पञ्चमी लेता है।

prompt.en: Join each phrase to its meaning.
prompt.hi: हर वाक्यांश को उसके अर्थ से जोड़िए।

explain.en: The fifth case: source, fear, protection, comparison.

prompt.en: Tap every word in the fifth case.
prompt.hi: पञ्चमी वाले हर शब्द को छुइए।

prompt.en: Say it like the small girl: “I fear the thunder.”
prompt.hi: नन्ही बालिका की तरह कहिए: ‘मैं गर्जन से डरती हूँ।’

explain.en: {{अहं मेघात् बिभेमि}}: the thing feared is in the fifth case.
explain.hi: {{अहं मेघात् बिभेमि}}: जिससे डर है वह पञ्चमी में है।

success.en: “अहं मेघात् बिभेमि,” you say, and the little girl nods so hard her plait bounces. The Ācārya smiles. “And now say what protects you.” “आचार्यस्य गृहम्,” says Dādī softly. At the window the wind spirit goes still, listening.
success.hi: “अहं मेघात् बिभेमि,” आप कहते हैं, और नन्ही बालिका इतनी ज़ोर से सिर हिलाती है कि उसकी चोटी उछल जाती है। आचार्य मुस्कुराते हैं। “और अब कहो कि तुम्हें किसने बचाया है।” “आचार्यस्य गृहम्,” दादी धीमे से कहती हैं। खिड़की पर पवन-भूत शान्त होकर सुनने लगता है।

failure.en: The girl waits. What you fear goes in the fifth case: {{मेघात्}}.
failure.hi: बालिका प्रतीक्षा करती है। जिससे डरें वह पञ्चमी में: {{मेघात्}}।

text.en: What is feared: the fifth case.
